requirement: Skills plugins and custom slash commands

subtractedRequirementOwners.note: Client/UI ownership remains dependency-constrained and is not reassigned to EXT-001/002.

subtractedRequirementOwners.ownedPartition: bounded safe bundled-skill file extraction and materialization
skill invocation passes the same policy gate as tools

reviewedPartitions.inputs: ordered embedded, local-directory or remote-URL skill discovery sources plus agent permission context
reviewedPartitions.outputs: deduplicated SkillV2.Info list with later-source name precedence and permission-filtered availability
reviewedPartitions.failureSemantics: unreadable/invalid skill files are skipped; file glob/read failures are softened; remote discovery may fail through its discovery service
reviewedPartitions.stateLifetime: location-scoped transform state and an in-memory source-keyed loaded-skill cache
reviewedPartitions.resourceLifetime: filesystem traversal plus optional remote skill discovery; cache invalidation policy remains explicitly unresolved upstream
reviewedPartitions.ownershipBlocker: Both EXT-001 and EXT-002 have the same extensibility surface and identical REQ-017 story text; EXT-013 already owns safe bundled-file extraction and TOOL-007 owns skill policy gating.

reviewedPartitions.inputs: location-scoped command transform callbacks keyed by command name
reviewedPartitions.outputs: stable in-memory command lookup/list projection with later transform updates preserved
reviewedPartitions.failureSemantics: the reviewed registry has no transport/network failure path; State transform failures follow the shared State runtime semantics
reviewedPartitions.stateLifetime: location-scoped in-memory State transforms and command map
reviewedPartitions.resourceLifetime: bounded by registered command metadata in the owning location scope
reviewedPartitions.ownershipBlocker: The V2 runtime exposes command.list, but the config specification explicitly rejects separate user-authored command configuration; this may be internal/built-in runtime and is not task-bound to EXT-001 or EXT-002.

designCaveat.conclusion: V2 removes separate user-authored command configuration, places named reusable user workflows under skills, and leaves internal command routing/built-ins as runtime concerns. Therefore EXT-001/EXT-002 cannot be assigned as 'skills' versus 'custom commands' from requirement wording or task order.

disqualifiers: EXT-001 and EXT-002 have identical source-surface and requirement bindings.
SkillV2 mixes filesystem discovery, optional remote URL discovery, cache lifetime and permission filtering beyond a small pure registry.
Existing EXT-013 and TOOL-007 already own separate safe extraction and policy-gate behavior and must not be re-owned.
No task card, worklog or pinned task-specific spec binds CommandV2 to EXT-001 or EXT-002.
The V2 config design explicitly removes separate user-authored command configuration and moves reusable workflows to skills.
An easy in-memory implementation would invent custom-slash ownership if treated as a residual task solely because CommandV2 exists.

historyReview.limitation: The pinned OpenCode checkout is used only for current source/caller/test/spec contracts; missing historical intent is not used to assign EXT-001 versus EXT-002.

closureCriteria: Ownership must come from explicit task-specific source/path/spec evidence that distinguishes EXT-001 from EXT-002; task order, numeric IDs, residual requirement membership and surface arithmetic are never sufficient.
A candidate must specify inputs, outputs, failure semantics, state/resource lifetime and authority while excluding already-owned EXT-013/TOOL-007 behavior and dependency-constrained UI-010.

Any custom-command implementation must reconcile the pinned V2 design that removes separate user-authored command configuration and explain whether CommandV2 is internal runtime, user-visible slash behavior, or a different owning domain.
All six unresolved partitions must receive source-grounded task dispositions or remain blocked before REQ-017 extensibility ownership can be called decomposed.
